subject: SDLC control matrix + keystore rotation Q&A
messages:
From: Brad Cooper <brad.cooper@acmebank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: SOC2-Audit <audit@acmebank.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jul 2028 09:15:00 -0000
Subject: SDLC controls: keystore rotation + evidence ask

Irene,

Thanks for agreeing to help with the next tranche of SIG/SOC2 follow-ups. Our assessor has two immediate asks that we need artifacts for by EOD next Wednesday:

1) Keystore rotation policy and evidence that production signing keys and deployment keystores are rotated (or have a rotation schedule) and that rotations are logged and approved.
2) CI/CD gating: PR gate policy, how secrets are provisioned to runners/agents, and an example pipeline run (logs) that demonstrates the gating and ephemeral secret access.

Could you provide a short control matrix mapping (control -> artifact) plus the artifacts above? If you have an internal runbook or a short policy doc, that helps. Prefer PDFs or single XLSX for the matrix.

Appreciate it — auditor is focused on demonstrating technical controls end-to-end.

Brad
Brad Cooper
Senior IT Auditor, Acme Bank
brad.cooper@acmebank.com

Brad — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa and Jonas; they'll assemble the artifacts and provide the mapping.

Planned deliverables (target: Wed EOD):
- SDLC control matrix (control -> policy -> artifact) (sdlc_control_matrix_v1.xlsx)
- Keystore rotation schedule + CSV of last rotation events (rotation-schedule.csv)
- CI/CD policy and sample pipeline run (ci-pipeline-policy.md + pipeline run logs snapshot)

Marissa: can you confirm we can include an anonymized pipeline run log (redact tokens, IPs) to demonstrate ephemeral secret fetch and PR gating?
Jonas: can you add the short paragraph that explains how our keystore rotation is approved (who signs off) and where the logs are stored (audit bucket + KMS envelope metadata)?

If any of the artifacts need an access control note (e.g., link only accessible to Acme auditors), mention it and we'll create a share link.

Thanks —
Irene

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2028 08:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: SDLC controls: keystore rotation + evidence ask

Brad / team — attaching the artifacts listed below and a concise explanation of each control. I've redacted any sensitive runtime tokens from the pipeline logs before zipping.

Attachments included: 1) sdlc_control_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix mapping controls to artifacts), 2) ci-pipeline-policy.md (short policy for PR gating and secrets provisioning), 3) rotation-schedule.csv (keystore rotation events/metadata), 4) pr-gate-screenshots.pdf (screenshots of the PR gate in our repo).

Key points (brief):
- PR gating: All changes to production-serving repos require a PR that passes automated checks (lint/tests), a successful canary roll (when applicable), and an explicit approvals block from a designated owner team. Policy is enforced via branch protection rules and an OPA gate in the pipeline. Evidence: pr-gate-screenshots.pdf + branch protection snapshot in the matrix.
- Secrets provisioning: We do not store long-lived secrets in CI. Runners obtain ephemeral credentials via an OIDC flow to our Vault cluster. Vault issues short-lived tokens that are scoped to the job and auto-revoked on job completion. Evidence: pipeline run logs (redacted) show the OIDC exchange and the Vault token TTL. See ci-pipeline-policy.md for flow diagram and docs link.
- Keystore rotation: Production keystore (signing keyset) is rotated on a 90-day cadence or on-demand for incidents. Rotations are recorded in rotation-schedule.csv and require a rotation request that is reviewed by Security and the Release Manager; final approval is recorded in our audit log (audit-bucket path included in the matrix). KMS is used for envelope encryption, and we store key fingerprints and rotation metadata in the audit object.
- Auditability: Rotation events and Vault audit log entries are retained per our retention policy (90 days for live audit trail, 7 years for hashed/aggregated retention depending on control). We can provide a pointer to the audit S3/GCS path for reviewers with access.

Let me know if you want a short screencast demonstrating the run.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior DevOps Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Brad Cooper <brad.cooper@acmebank.com>

Thanks Jonas — this is exactly what we needed. Quick clarifying Qs from the assessor: 
1) You mentioned 90-day rotation cadence. Can you confirm whether any production signing keys are on an exception (longer than 90 days) and where the exception approvals are stored?
2) The retention windows you referenced — can you point us to the policy doc or clause in your retention schedule that covers the 90-day live audit trail vs. the long-term hashed retention?

If you can reply with two short bullets and a pointer to the retention policy doc (or include it), we'll close the ticket on our side. Great work.

Brad
